choice.quote: Your unarmed attack from bestial rage gains one of the following traits until you stop raging: backswing, forceful, parry, razing, or sweep.
choice.reason: engineFieldsPresent is empty and the id appears nowhere in src/ — not in content.modes (225 entries), not in content.stances (129), and not in any of featGrants/featGrantsAuto/featGrantsLane/featPickGrants/featFeatGrants/FEAT_SITUATIONAL. choice.quote: Whenever you would gain a benefit from a psychic amp, you can have the amp affect the tethered creature instead.
choice.reason: Owner's ruling F: the benefit is redirected to an ALLY, not gained by you, so nothing on your sheet moves — and 'Choose a willing creature within 60 feet' is a choice of TARGET, not a build-time choice. The feat adds no number, resource, or defence of its own.

choice.quote: You gain the Base Kinesis impulse.
choice.reason: The impulse it hands you DOES ship (classFeatures/base-kinesis, actionCost 2 actions, and actions/base-kinesis), but the FEAT record carries no grants/grantsFeats/grantedFeatId, its own actionCost is {type:'passive'}, and 'base-kinesis' is absent from FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS in src/rules/featGrants*.ts / featFeatGrants.ts. MainTab.tsx:195-198 builds the Actions list from character.feats filtered by isActionCost, so a passive feat contributes no action row, and class-feature actions are never collected there at all.

choice.suggestedField: FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS in src/rules/featFeatGrants.ts (or `grantsFeats` on the record) pointing at the base-kinesis impulse, since the target record already exists

This feat has no innateSpells, so the Heal never reaches the Spells page and its level-scaled rank is never computed. ('Select up to five creatures to remain unaffected' is target selection and needs nothing.)

choice.quote: **Frequency** once per day
choice.reason: The record carries limitedUses {max:1,per:'day'}, which is live for feats: effectiveUses/featUse in src/rules/featUses.ts, rendered as spendable pips at src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:289-320. choice.reason: Every printed effect is on the record and wired: abilityBoosts [{choice:[cha,wis]},{free}], trainedSkill:'nature', trainedLore:'plane-of-earth', grantedFeatId:'natural-medicine'. natural-medicine carries no sub-choice of its own (checked in core.json), so nothing further is owed. Calling this merely 'examined' understated it.

choice.quote: You're trained in the Athletics skill and the Ocean Lore skill. You gain the Underwater Marauder skill feat.
choice.reason: abilityBoosts [{choice:[con,dex]},{free}], trainedSkill:'athletics', trainedLore:'ocean', grantedFeatId:'underwater-marauder' — all four printed effects present, and underwater-marauder has no sub-choice in core.json. The 'Prerequisite Region' line is GM/campaign framing with no sheet number.

choice.quote: When you choose your eidolon, you also determine its appearance and general form, within the parameters for that particular type of eidolon.
choice.reason: engineFieldsPresent is empty on the classFeature, but the feature is modelled through the class + companion systems, not a field: 'Choose a type of eidolon' IS the summoner subclass picker (13 options in classes.summoner.subclass.options, each with tradition + grants.skills), and the eidolon is materialised as a companion — companions.ts:672-697 gives it its own ability mods, its own Dex-capped unarmored AC, primary/secondary unarmed Strikes on eidolonAttackRank, shared HP, and senses; companionGrants.ts carries the per-type senses/speeds/strike riders (angel-eidolon, beast-eidolon, airborne-form, …); build.ts:3070-3078 injects one for the Summoner-Dedication archetype. This is one of the most heavily wired records in the sample.

choice.quote: you can also choose a skill in which you are already trained and become an expert in that skill
choice.reason: The `choice` field {flag:'longevitySkill', prompt:'Skill', kind:'skills'} is present, so the pick IS offered and recorded (FeatsTab.tsx:61 renders 'Expert Longevity (Athletics)'). But the flag is consumed nowhere — grep for 'longevitySkill' across src/ returns no hits — and the app has no mechanism for a temporary proficiency-RANK change at all (mode modifiers carry only flat typed values, never a rank; content.modes has no rank-changing entry). So the pick is cosmetic.

choice.quote: Choose one of your attuned apparitions; for 10 minutes, you gain a fly Speed equal to your land Speed and resistance to precision damage equal to your level, but your chosen apparition is dispersed for the duration
choice.reason: limitedUses {max:1,per:'hour'} is present, so the frequency is tracked — but nothing else is. The pick is answerable: attuned apparitions are real build data (build.extraChoices['apparition'], build.ts:1890). And modes cannot cover it even if one existed — no mode in content.modes carries a speed modifier (0 of 225) and the four that mention resistance do so only in a prose `note`.

The engine has the right field for this — `grantedFeatByChoice`, documented in types.ts:595-601 as fixing exactly 'they all handed out the FIRST branch's feat whatever you picked' — and five backgrounds use it (conservator, dedicated-delver, anti-thrune-saboteur, historical-reenactor, aon-historical-reeanactor). glory-hound is not one of them, and backgroundGrantedFeats (build.ts:331-345) therefore falls through to the flat grant.

choice.quote: The enemy must choose one of the following options.
choice.reason: The dismissal folds two different things into the "HP/damage" ruling. The Refuse damage (2d6→6d6) and the prone are indeed target-side and need nothing — but "your Strikes against it deal 1 extra spirit damage until the end of your next turn (2 at 9th, 3 at 16th)" is a bonus on YOUR OWN damage rolls, i.e. a row in your Strike breakdown, and that lane is fully built and populated. src/rules/derive.ts:1195-1215 (strikeDamageRiders) pulls `strikeDamage` from db.feats AND db.classFeatures — classFeatures/spirit-striking and greater-spirit-striking use it today ({type:'spirit', byStrikeProficiency:…, note:'Spirit Striking'}). For the CONDITIONAL, temporary version the app uses a mode: ModeTargetKind includes 'damage' (types.ts:1339-1349) and ModeModifier.appliesWhen makes it conditional (types.ts:1357-1359); 11 entries in content.modes already do precisely Iron Command's shape — item-chivalric-emblem {target:'damage', type:'circumstance', value:1, appliesWhen:'with the emblazoned weapon, against the creature that damaged your ally'} and item-grudgestone {target:'damage', type:'status', value:3, appliesWhen:'on Strikes with the affixed weapon against the creature that critically hit you'}. Iron Command is in none of it: I checked all 225 content.modes keys, all 129 stances, and grepped 'iron-command' across src/ — no hits; the classFeature carries only actionCost {type:'reaction'}. The cause link cited as cover is descRefs on classes.champion.subclass.options.obedience (label 'Iron Command', key 'actions') — a description hyperlink, not a registry, and the Obedience option carries no grants at all.
choice.whatIsMissing: The +1/+2/+3 spirit damage the champion's own Strikes gain after the reaction fires never appears anywhere: no damage row, no star, no toggle. It is the Obedience champion's only recurring personal buff and it is invisible, while the structurally identical Chivalric Emblem and Grudgestone riders are modelled.
choice.suggestedField: a content.modes entry (target 'damage', appliesWhen 'against the creature your Iron Command triggered on, until the end of your next turn'), or `strikeDamage` on the classFeature the way spirit-striking does — level scaling 1/2/3 at 1st/9th/16th

choice.quote: You gain the Specialty Crafting skill feat.

Background-granted feats get no choice value (build.ts:2045-2048) and no picker (Builder.tsx:1114-1129 renders name + ChoiceDetails; shared.tsx:2465-2471 renders the name). It also degrades a live display: FEAT_SITUATIONAL['specialty-crafting'] (situationalBonuses.ts:342) stars Crafting with when 'to Craft items of your chosen specialty'.

choice.suggestedField: a picker for background-granted feats' own `choice` on the Setup background SubCard (shared.tsx, alongside the existing Background skill / Background Lore SubCards) — pending task #41

choice.quote: Choose one skill. You temporarily increase your proficiency rank with that skill by one step for 1 minute (from untrained to trained, trained to expert, and expert to master).
choice.reason: limitedUses {max:1,per:'day'} is present and live, but that is all: no `choice`, no `effectChoices`, and the id appears nowhere in src/ (no mode, no stance, no registry). The text states the increase 'adjusts your proficiency bonus', so a real sheet number should move for a full minute, and the app has no rank-changing mechanism anywhere (mode modifiers carry flat typed values only).

choice.quote: Whenever you can clearly identify the stars, if you roll a success on a check to Sense Direction or otherwise orienteer, you get a critical success instead; if you roll a critical failure at such a check, you get a failure instead.
choice.reason: The record carries abilityBoosts + trainedSkill:'survival' (correctly no granted feat — the text prints none), but the conditional benefit is unmodelled: 'nocturnal-navigator' is absent from FEAT_SITUATIONAL and the record has no `situational` field. This lane is fully built and open to backgrounds — explain.ts:188-206 characterSituationalIds pushes c.backgroundId, 31 background ids are already registered (ex-con-token-guard, godless-graycloak, sun-dancer, tide-watcher, …), and degree-of-success upgrades are expressible: 17 registry entries use that phrasing, e.g. "breath-control": when 'against inhaled threats (success becomes critical success)'.
choice.whatIsMissing: Survival carries no * and its detail popup lists nothing, so the player has no indication their Sense Direction successes upgrade to critical successes under the stars.
choice.suggestedField: FEAT_SITUATIONAL in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts, keyed 'nocturnal-navigator', targets [{kind:'skill', detail:'survival'}]

choice.quote: **Frequency** six times per day (but only once per day per color)
choice.reason: The verdict quotes the frequency line "six times per day (but only once per day per color)" and then declares the footprint complete, but the record models only the first half of that sentence: counters is a single {id:'freq', label:'per day', max:6, per:'day', resetsOnRest:true}. The per-colour restriction — restated in the effect text as "Select one of the six colors of the cube that hasn't been activated today", with the failure branch turning on which colours are already spent — has no storage. This is not a shape the app lacks: 31 items carry more than two counters and the pattern for exactly this case is in the data. holy-prayer-beads-greater uses one NAMED counter per effect ([{id:'bless',label:'Bless',max:1},{id:'divine-wrath',…},{id:'heal',…},{id:'cleanse-affliction',…}]) and dragons-eye-charm carries four separate {max:1, per:'day'} counters (freq…freq4) for four independent once-a-day uses. So six 1/day counters labelled Red…Indigo is the established idiom, and the mode side of the verdict is right (all six benefits read "Allies in the area", modifiers:[] with the owner's ruling in the note) — the resource side is not.
choice.whatIsMissing: Nothing on the sheet records WHICH colours have been used today. The six pips are interchangeable, so the tracker happily lets the player activate Red six times, and after a couple of activations there is no way to tell which sides have darkened to violet.
choice.suggestedField: replace the single 6/day counter with six named per-day counters on the item record (Red/Orange/Yellow/Green/Blue/Indigo, each max 1, per 'day', resetsOnRest true) — the holy-prayer-beads-greater / dragons-eye-charm pattern

choice.quote: The GM rolls a secret check using the bonus of the propagandist against the DC required to Gather Information on the given subject of the propaganda.
choice.reason: This is a downtime SERVICE the GM adjudicates — the roll is the propagandist's, made secretly by the GM, and the outcome moves public opinion in a settlement, not a number on your sheet. The one thing the app does owe it, the purchase price, is present (price {gp:15}, itemType 'equipment'). The body text is also an AoN umbrella listing all seven levels' prices, which under the owner's ruling A is summary matter rather than seven ownable things.

choice.quote: **Requirements** There's at least one soul stored in the reaper's grasp
choice.reason: engineFieldsPresent is empty: the item has activationCost but no `counters` and no `frequency`, so the 10-soul pool that GATES both activations has nowhere to live. The app tracks exactly this kind of pool elsewhere — paradigm-cube (same sample) carries counters, and itemUses.ts renders pips on the inventory row. The 'damage/HP needs nothing' ruling does not reach this: call-worm-spirit in this same sample is pure damage and still carries a tracked limitedUses, so a resource tracker is in-scope for damage abilities by the app's own precedent.
choice.whatIsMissing: No pip row or counter for stored souls, so the player has no on-sheet way to know whether either activation's Requirements are met (and no place to record the soul levels the damage/temp-HP formulas read).
choice.suggestedField: `counters` on the item record (max 10), the same field paradigm-cube and spear-of-the-destroyers-flame already use

choice.quote: You're trained in the Occultism skill and the Herbalism Lore skill. You gain the Root Magic skill feat.
choice.reason: abilityBoosts [{choice:[int,wis]},{free}], trainedSkill:'occultism', trainedLore:'herbalism', grantedFeatId:'root-magic' — all four printed effects on the record, and root-magic carries no sub-choice in core.json, so the flat grant is correct. Nothing outstanding.

choice.quote: You're trained in the Survival skill and a Lore skill related to one terrain you scouted in (such as Forest Lore or Cavern Lore).
choice.reason: The open-ended Lore is explicitly handled: trainedLoreChoice:true (documented at types.ts:579-582) drives a free-text Lore field in the builder at shared.tsx:2513-2531, stored in BuildState.backgroundLore and trained as lore:<typed>. Plus abilityBoosts, trainedSkill:'survival' and grantedFeatId:'forager' (forager has no sub-choice). This is one of the seven records task #9 was built for.

choice.quote: You're trained in the Crafting skill and the Shory Lore skill. You gain the Specialty Crafting skill feat.
choice.reason: Same defect as local-scion: grantedFeatId:'specialty-crafting' whose own choice {flag:'specialtyCrafting', kind:'array'} is an unpinned player pick, and background-granted feats never receive a choice value (build.ts:2045-2048) nor a picker (Builder.tsx:1114-1129, shared.tsx:2465-2471). The background's own three effects (abilityBoosts, trainedSkill:'crafting', trainedLore:'shory') are all correctly present — the gap is only the granted feat's sub-pick.
choice.whatIsMissing: The Crafting specialty is never chosen, so the Crafting star's note (FEAT_SITUATIONAL['specialty-crafting'], situationalBonuses.ts:342) says 'your chosen specialty' with nothing chosen.
choice.suggestedField: a picker for background-granted feats' own `choice` on the Setup background SubCard (shared.tsx) — pending task #41

choice.quote: While the *Spear of the Destroyer's Flame* is in your possession, you gain fire resistance 20.
choice.reason: The deciding line is genuinely wired, not just stored: passiveEffects {resistances:[{type:'fire', value:20}]} is read at derive.ts:709-711, which pushes pe.resistances into the character's defence sources for any worn/invested/equipped item. The 1/day Commander-of-Flame activation is covered by frequency {max:1,per:'day'} plus counters [{id:'freq',...},{id:'freq2', per:'week', resetsOnRest:false}]. Everything remaining — commanding the Army of Fire, the army's +10 Speed and quickened condition — is bonuses on OTHER creatures (ruling F) and GM-adjudicated army play.

choice.quote: You gain the Trick Magic Item skill feat, as well as the Opportunistic Accusation reaction.
choice.reason: grantedFeatId:'trick-magic-item' covers the first half. The second does not arrive: 'opportunistic-accusation' exists in core.json as an ACTION (actions/opportunistic-accusation) but there is no feat by that id, and grantedFeatId/grantsFeats resolve against content.feats (build.ts:2045-2048, FeatsTab.tsx:117 `content.feats[gid]`), so the reaction can't be pointed at. It also cannot reach the Actions list on its own — MainTab.tsx:195-198 builds featActions from character.feats only.
choice.whatIsMissing: The Opportunistic Accusation reaction is simply not granted: it appears nowhere in Feats & Features and nowhere in the Actions list, so the player loses a reaction the background prints.
choice.suggestedField: either a feat-shaped record for opportunistic-accusation plus grantedFeatId:['trick-magic-item','opportunistic-accusation'] (grantedFeatId already accepts string[], types.ts:594), or a granted-action lane in MainTab's action collection

choice.quote: When you select this feat, choose a demesne, an area of no more than 2,000 square feet.
choice.reason: The pick is a place in the world, not an option on your sheet, and everything it produces lives on that place: a permanent Peaceful Bubble on the area, three unseen custodians attending it, and an elemental sentinel on one object in it. None is a spell you cast, a resource you spend, or a number on your character — it is a GM-adjudicated standing feature of a location (and 'you must legitimately own the area' is explicitly a GM question). Nothing in the app's vocabulary would hold it without inventing a location sheet.

choice.quote: You're trained in the Athletics skill and the Dragon Lore skill. You gain the Titan Wrestler skill feat.
choice.reason: abilityBoosts [{choice:[cha,str]},{free}], trainedSkill:'athletics', trainedLore:'dragon', grantedFeatId:'titan-wrestler' — every printed effect present, and titan-wrestler carries no sub-choice in core.json. The '[Legacy - Age of Ashes]' marker and the shard-of-Dahak framing are narrative; rarity:'rare' is recorded.

choice.quote: When you emerge and make your daily preparations, you can select a different surki heritage to replace it.
choice.reason: engineFieldsPresent is empty and the id appears nowhere in src/. The pick is fully answerable from existing data — four surki heritages ship (breaker/elytron/hardshell/lantern-surki), secondary-adaptation already models a surki-heritage pick as choice {flag:'secondSurkiHeritage', kind:'array'} with those four options, and grand-metamorphosis models the evolution pick with eight options — and the app has a purpose-built lane for nightly re-picks: src/rules/dailyChoices.ts, driven entirely by `choice.daily = true` ('Choices re-made at DAILY PREPARATIONS … wiring a new feat is a data edit, not a code edit').
choice.whatIsMissing: The nightly heritage swap (and the matching evolution re-pick) is never offered, so the player cannot change which surki heritage is active without editing the build — and no heritage benefit ever moves.
choice.suggestedField: `choice` with daily:true on the feat (src/rules/dailyChoices.ts), reusing secondary-adaptation's four heritage options plus grand-metamorphosis's evolution options

choice.quote: Once per day, you can spend an Interact action to merge with your ward and heal Hit Points equal to your level.
choice.reason: The record carries limitedUses {max:1,per:'day'} — but that field is DEAD on a background. featUses.ts:83-93 iterates c.feats only and reads db.feats[f.featId]; FeatsTab.tsx:295 draws pips from content.feats[e.featId]; grepping every limitedUses consumer in src/ turns up no backgrounds/heritages path, and backgrounds are not rows in the Feats list at all. Only two backgrounds carry the field (warded-by-kami, wished-alive), so both are inert. The healing itself needs nothing (HP), and the ward's animal/plant/object/location is narrative — the tracker is the one real thing owed, and it is not delivered.
choice.whatIsMissing: No use pips anywhere for the 1/day ward-merge: the field is stored, shows nothing, and can never be spent or refilled on rest.
choice.suggestedField: extend featUses.ts (featUses/effectiveUses) to scan the background/heritage records the way explain.ts:188-206 already does for situational ids, so background limitedUses reaches the FeatsTab pip control

situational.quote: **Frequency** once per day **Trigger** An animal within 30 feet wearing the paired blinders attempts a saving throw against a fear effect but hasn't rolled yet
situational.reason: core.json items.abidance-blinders carries counters ([{id:'freq',label:'per day',max:1,per:'day',resetsOnRest:true}]) and frequency ({max:1,per:'day'}), so the one-per-day activation is tracked. Everything else in the text lands on a domesticated animal that explicitly "doesn't have combat training or the minion trait" — not your companion and not on your sheet — and the +1 status bonus is that animal's save (ruling F).

situational.quote: Alignment Ampoule (Major) ... Price 3,000 gp Bulk L You gain a +3 item bonus to attack rolls. The bomb deals 3d4 damage and 4 splash damage.
situational.reason: core.json items.alignment-ampoule-major has engine fields = none AND itemType 'equipment' with no category/group/damage/range, so deriveStrike (src/rules/derive.ts:1235 `if (!item || item.itemType !== 'weapon') return null;` and :1239 `if (!w.damage) return null;`) rejects it outright. Separately, no bomb anywhere carries an attack-bonus field (grep of core.json items for attackBonus/itemAttackBonus/bombBonus = 0 hits) and the strike attack item bonus is only `Math.max(abpOn(c) ? abpAttack(c.level) : runes?.potency ?? 0, mpRef?.attack ?? 0)` (derive.ts:1277) — a consumable bomb has no runes, so the graded +1/+2/+3 can never be added. Not in FEAT_SITUATIONAL, not in the modes bucket (only 3 bomb-ish modes exist: grudgestone, grudgestone-greater, statue-skin-salve), not in stances.
situational.suggestedField: items.alignment-ampoule-major: weapon typing (itemType/category/group/damage/range) plus an intrinsic attack item-bonus field folded into the `potencyBonus` max at src/rules/derive.ts:1277 (or a FEAT_SITUATIONAL strikeAttack entry as the display-only fallback)
situational.whatIsMissing: A 17th-level, 3,000 gp bomb that produces no Strike at all — no attack roll, no damage line — and whose printed +3 item bonus to attack rolls exists nowhere in the app.

situational.quote: The armor grants a +4 item bonus to saving throws to the wearer.

proficiency.quote: You rally a creature within 30 feet in an attempt to reduce its frightened or stupefied condition.
proficiency.reason: Everything it changes is a condition value on ANOTHER creature — an ally or a target, not you (owner's ruling F plus the 'changes a number on the TARGET' exclusion). Your own Diplomacy modifier and DCs are untouched; the roll is against 'the saving throw DC of the effect that caused the condition', which the GM supplies. The rank-scaling condition list (master adds clumsy/enfeebled, legendary adds stunned) only widens what you may target.

proficiency.quote: You gain the Electrified Crystal Ward focus spell, and you are trained in arcane spell attack rolls and spell DCs. Your spellcasting ability is Intelligence.
proficiency.reason: The focus SPELL half is wired (feats.crystal-ward-spells.focusSpells = ['electrified-crystal-ward'], picked up as featFocusSpells at build.ts:1903 and worth a pool point at build.ts:1966). The PROFILE half is not: unlike its sibling suns-fury, this record carries no spellcastingGrant, and the engine could not use one anyway — the focus entry is constructed at build.ts:1940-1951 with a hardcoded proficiency 'trained' and with focusTradition/focusKey resolved only from grantOptions, the class's own spellcasting block, or the class-keyed FOCUS_CASTING table (build.ts:1265, which holds only champion/monk/ranger), falling through to `focusCls.keyAbility[0]`. spellcastingGrants are not even collected until build.ts:2511, after the focus entry is built, and are then applied only to the 'innate-casting' entry (build.ts:2777). Crystal Keeper is not in CASTER_ARCHETYPES either.
proficiency.whatIsMissing: On any non-caster host the Electrified Crystal Ward spell attack roll and Focus DC are computed from the wrong attribute and tradition — a fighter (classes.fighter.keyAbility[0] === 'dex') gets a Dexterity-keyed, 'occult' focus DC instead of the Intelligence-keyed, arcane one the feat grants. The Focus DC tile and the spell's attack number are wrong, not merely absent.
proficiency.suggestedField: spellcastingGrant {tradition:'arcane', keyAbility:'int', proficiency:'trained'} on core.json feats.crystal-ward-spells, PLUS routing it into the focus entry: move the spellcastingGrants collection (build.ts:2511) above the focus-entry construction (build.ts:1940) and let it override focusTradition/focusKey/proficiency.

proficiency.quote: Choose one 1st-rank spell and one 2nd-rank spell from those listed for a dragon spellcaster of your draconic benefactor's type
proficiency.reason: Carries both effectChoices (two open spell pickers, ids dracomancer-rank1/rank2, each spellFilter {rank, grantAs:'innate', innate:{usesPerDay:1}}) and spellcastingGrant {arcane, cha, trained}. The open-spell picker lane is src/rules/spellChoice.ts + openChoice.ts and the grant is applied at build.ts:2515/2777. proficiency.reason: A GM-adjudicated exploration-subsystem permission with no number on your sheet, and what it grants belongs to the GROUP's hexploration budget, not to you (the 'downtime permission' and 'bonus goes to the party, not your sheet' exclusions). No modifier, proficiency, use pool or pick is implied for the character.

proficiency.reason: Registered in the skill-action registry: src/rules/skillActions.ts:744-750 has {name:'Fascinating Performance', minRank:'trained', feat:true, featName:'Fascinating Performance'} under performance, and StatDetailModal.tsx:54-55 gates feat-flagged skill actions on the character's owned feat NAMES, so it appears in the Performance breakdown once you own it (the rank-scaling observer count is spelled out in its desc). Its id is also a grant target in featFeatGrants.ts:198,241.

proficiency.quote: The enemy must roll its attack twice and take the lower result.
proficiency.reason: The whole effect is a misfortune effect on the ENEMY's attack roll against an ALLY — a number on the target, not on you (the 'changes a number on the TARGET' exclusion). 'You're trained in snapping and fluttering your fans' is flavour prose, not a proficiency grant, and the two-fan requirement is a wielding condition the player reads off their own inventory.

proficiency.quote: Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in a given weapon or weapons, you also gain that proficiency in the dogslicer, horsechopper, and all goblin weapons in which you are trained.
proficiency.reason: This is precisely the `weaponFamiliarity.mirrorBestCategory` grant shape (featGrants.ts:110-119, consumed at build.ts:2453-2468, `const rank = wf.mirrorBestCategory ? bestCategory : wf.rank`) and the id is registered NOWHERE. Grepped src/ and scripts/: 'goblin-weapon-expertise' appears in no registry, and core.json feats.goblin-weapon-expertise has no engine fields at all (keys: id, name, traits, rarity, source, description, level, category, edition). Its hobgoblin twin IS registered (featGrantsAuto.ts:154), as are catfolk, conrasu, genie, ghoran, grippli, kobold, vanara and vishkanya — the core-ancestry set (dwarven, elven, gnome, goblin) was skipped. The prerequisite Goblin Weapon Familiarity is likewise unregistered: core.json feats.goblin-weapon-familiarity carries only critSpec fields, no weaponFamiliarity.
proficiency.whatIsMissing: A 13th-level goblin fighter with this feat still shows trained (not expert/master/legendary) with dogslicer and horsechopper — the attack modifier on those weapon Strikes never rises with the class's martial rank. The prerequisite feat does not even grant the initial trained proficiency.
proficiency.suggestedField: src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts FEAT_GRANTS_AUTO — 'goblin-weapon-expertise': { weaponFamiliarity: { weapons: ['dogslicer','horsechopper', ...goblin-trait weapons], mirrorBestCategory: true } }, and 'goblin-weapon-familiarity' with rank:'trained' (mirroring featGrantsAuto.ts:154's hobgoblin entry).

proficiency.quote: When you make your daily preparations, you can either gain the expert proficiency rank in one skill in which you're untrained or raise your proficiency rank to master in one skill in which you're trained or better.
proficiency.reason: The daily-preparation lane exists and is data-driven — src/rules/dailyChoices.ts:10 says 'A record opts in with `choice.daily = true`; everything here is driven by that flag' — and dailyChoicesFor() explicitly scans owned feats (dailyChoices.ts:41). core.json feats.haunting-memories carries no `choice` at all (keys: descRefs, actionCost, archetype only) and the id appears in no registry. So the Rest sheet never asks the question. This is not the ally/target/GM/narrative case: the text names an exact proficiency RANK on the player's own sheet, plus a bonus skill feat.
proficiency.whatIsMissing: Every morning the player should pick a skill and see it jump to expert (from untrained) or master (from trained+), and pick a matching skill feat. Neither pick is offered and neither number moves. Note the pick alone would not be enough: dailyChoices answers are stored in PlayState.dailyChoices (play.ts:73) and are read only by CharacterSheet.tsx for display — nothing feeds them into derive, so no existing daily choice changes a proficiency rank.
proficiency.suggestedField: core.json feats.haunting-memories.choice = {flag:'hauntingSkill', daily:true, kind:'array'|'open', prompt:'...'} for the pick, plus a new path from PlayState.dailyChoices into the skill-rank computation (today PlayState.dailyChoices has no derive consumer at all) and a second daily choice for the granted skill feat.

proficiency.quote: The GM determines the DC of any check required and the amount of time your work requires (usually at least a day or two of downtime).
proficiency.reason: Textbook GM-adjudicated downtime with no number on your sheet — the record itself hands the DC and the duration to the GM, and the outcome is narrative ('you can hope for certain effects, such as easier hunts or birds falling silent'). The legendary clause only shortens the time. No modifier, use pool or pick.

proficiency.quote: Your proficiency rank for your kineticist class DC increases to expert.
proficiency.reason: Registered in the advancement table: src/rules/advancement.ts:437 has { level: 7, track: 'classDc', rank: 'expert', source: 'kinetic-expertise' }, so the kineticist class DC actually rises to expert at 7th and the breakdown attributes it to this feature by name.

proficiency.quote: When you Subsist during downtime, the DC for your skill check is reduced by 2.
proficiency.reason: A -2 to the Subsist DC is exactly what FEAT_SITUATIONAL already encodes for a dozen sibling records, and this id is in no registry (grep of src/ returns nothing for 'like-a-roach'; core.json feats.like-a-roach carries only descRefs + actionCost). Compare situationalBonuses.ts:120 city-scavenger ({skill:'society'},{skill:'survival'}, when 'to Subsist...', '+1 circumstance'), :2173 scavenger-strix, :1968 treedweller-goblin, and especially :1773 emperors-peak-quartz-bracelet, whose third target encodes the exact same '-5 penalty' clause as a bonus string: when 'on a Survival check to Subsist after 8 hours or less of exploration', bonus '−2 penalty instead of −5'. The pattern is shipped; this record was skipped.
proficiency.whatIsMissing: No star/conditional-bonus row on Survival (or Society) for Subsist — the player sees no trace of the -2 DC reduction, of the waived minimum-proficiency requirement, or of the waived -5 penalty for subsisting after ≤8 hours of exploration.
proficiency.suggestedField: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts FEAT_SITUATIONAL — 'like-a-roach': targets [{kind:'skill', detail:'survival'}, {kind:'skill', detail:'society'}], when 'to Subsist during downtime (no minimum proficiency rank required; no −5 penalty after 8 hours or less of exploration)', bonus '+2 circumstance (DC reduced by 2)' — modelled on the emperors-peak-quartz-bracelet entry at situationalBonuses.ts:1773.

proficiency.quote: Your animal companion grows up, becoming a mature animal companion. Increase its proficiency rank in Performance to expert instead of one of the three skill increases for mature.
proficiency.reason: The companion-modification lane covers this shape exactly — COMPANION_MODS in src/rules/companionGrants.ts:143 supports maturityFloor (types at :134, applied at companions.ts:345-346: `if (MATURITY_RANK[mod.maturityFloor] > MATURITY_RANK[maturity]) maturity = mod.maturityFloor`) and skillGrants (:138). Grep confirms the id appears in no src/ file.
proficiency.whatIsMissing: The companion stat block stays at the 'young' rung: no +1 Str/Dex/Con/Wis from mature, unarmed Strikes stay at one damage die instead of two (companions.ts:78 tracks 'young 1 → mature/nimble/savage 2'), the mature Perception/save increases are absent, and Performance is not raised to expert. Every one of those is a printed number on the Companions tab.
proficiency.suggestedField: src/rules/companionGrants.ts COMPANION_MODS — 'mature-trained-companion': { kinds:['animal'], maturityFloor:'mature', skillGrants:[{skill:'performance', rank:'expert'}], note:'...Mesmerizing Performance advanced maneuver in place of the type's normal one' } (same shape as the 'chorus-companion' and 'paragon-companion' entries).

proficiency.quote: The shield has Hardness 6, HP 110, and BT 55.
proficiency.reason: engineFieldsPresent is empty only because shield stats live outside that vocabulary — core.json items.mycoweave-shield-major actually carries itemType 'shield', acBonus 2, hardness 6, hp 110, brokenThreshold 55, speedPenalty 0, activationCost {type:'reaction'}, i.e. every number the sheet shows for a shield and uses for Shield Block. proficiency.quote: the piano grants you a +2 item bonus to Performance checks made with it. The piano also provides access to composition spells based on your Performance proficiency rank, as if you had the corresponding feat.
proficiency.reason: Both halves are wired: FEAT_SITUATIONAL 'phantom-piano' at situationalBonuses.ts:1488 ({skill:'performance'}, when 'on Performance checks made using the piano itself…', '+2 item'), and core.json items.phantom-piano carries heldSpells (the six composition spells by rank), frequency {max:1, per:'day'} and counters [{id:'freq', resetsOnRest:true}] for the 'You gain 1 Focus Point' activation. Caveat: heldSpells is keyed by SPELL rank, not by Performance proficiency, so the trained/expert/master/legendary gating in the text is not enforced — a trained bard is offered Soothing Ballad. That is an over-grant, not a missing number.

proficiency.quote: For you, the Repair activity loses the exploration trait and takes 1 minute instead of 10 minutes.
proficiency.reason: Registered in the skill-action registry: src/rules/skillActions.ts:322-328 under crafting, {name:'Quick Repair', costText:'varies', minRank:'trained', feat:true, featName:'Quick Repair'} with a desc spelling out the 1 minute / 3 actions / 1 action ladder. StatDetailModal.tsx:55 renders feat-flagged skill actions for the skill's rank filtered by the character's owned feat names, so owning the feat changes what the Crafting breakdown prints. Nothing here is a stat modifier — only the Repair activity's time, which is where the app shows it.

proficiency.quote: you become trained in Crafting and Cooking Lore, and you gain the Improvise Tool skill feat.
proficiency.reason: Three flat grants, none of which reach the sheet, and the repo says so itself: core.json heritages.respite-of-a-thousand-roofs carries dataWarning 'Part of this effect references content missing from the current data — apply it manually. (FEAT_GRANTS: id not in feats/classFeatures)' and no trainedSkill/trainedSkills/loreChoices/grantsFeats. Verified in build.ts: FEAT_GRANTS is read only as FEAT_GRANTS[fc.featId] over `feats` (build.ts:2258, 2462), and heritages are consulted for a fixed short list only — heritageSkill (:1322), loreChoices (:1315), grantsFeats (:2190), grantsGeneralFeat (:2054), choiceResistance, grantedStrikes (:1019), effectChoices (:2444), FEAT_PICK_GRANTS (:2173). Worse, the featFeatGrants.ts:244 entry 'respite-of-a-thousand-roofs': ['improvise-tool'] can never fire: the FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS queue is seeded from `feats.map(f => f.featId)` (build.ts:2222) and the only other seeding path (build.ts:1544-1547) guards on `content.feats[id]`, so a heritage id never enters either queue.
proficiency.whatIsMissing: Crafting is not trained, Cooking Lore does not exist on the skill list, and Improvise Tool never appears in Feats & Features — three sheet entries absent. The player also gets no picker, because these are flat grants, not choices.
proficiency.suggestedField: Either extend the heritage lane so FEAT_GRANTS/FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS keys resolve for heritage ids (seed build.ts:2222's queue and the build.ts:2258 grant loop with build.heritageId), or express it on the record: heritages.respite-of-a-thousand-roofs.trainedSkills ['crafting'], trainedLore ['cooking'], grantsFeats ['improvise-tool'] — grantsFeats for a heritage IS already honoured at build.ts:2190.

proficiency.quote: the affixed weapon gains the holy trait for the triggering attack and all other attacks for 1 minute.
proficiency.reason: core.json items.sakuras-sprig carries uses {current:1, max:1} (consumable talisman, tracked through src/rules/itemUses.ts) plus activationCost. The remaining effect adds the holy trait to a weapon, which changes only what damage the weapon deals against unholy targets — covered by the owner's ruling that HP/damage never move sheet stats — and the trigger/requirement is a table-time condition the player reads off their own inventory.

proficiency.quote: You gain a +3 item bonus to Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation and Performance checks.
proficiency.reason: Doubly wired: FEAT_SITUATIONAL 'silvertongue-mutagen-greater' at situationalBonuses.ts:1805 encodes all ten targets (+3 item to the four social skills, -2 item to Arcana/Crafting/Occultism/Society/lore:*, and the Recall Knowledge critical-failure clause), the core.json modes bucket has item-silvertongue-mutagen-greater (duration '1 hour', with a note listing exactly the residuals it cannot encode), and the item carries uses {current:1, max:1}. The one thing left out is acknowledged in that mode note: 'Choose one skill you are trained in; you become untrained in it for the duration' has no picker, because a mode modifier cannot target a player-chosen skill.

proficiency.quote: You can cast Silence on yourself as a 2nd-rank innate occult spell and as a 1st-rank innate occult spell, each once per day. You also can cast Figment as an innate occult cantrip.
proficiency.reason: innateSpells is present, but one of its three grants is silently discarded, so only two of the feat's three castings reach the sheet. core.json feats.sound-mirror.innateSpells is [figment(atWill), silence(rank 1, 1/day), silence(rank 2, 1/day)] — two grants with the SAME spellId. build.ts:2740-2741 dedupes by spellId alone: `const innate = innateGrants.filter((g) => content.spells[g.spellId] && !seenInnate.has(g.spellId) && seenInnate.add(g.spellId))`. The first silence wins, so the rank-2 grant is dropped before castRank/innateUses ever see it, and innateUses only ever records `usesPerDay` from the surviving grant (which is 1). The data was authored correctly; the engine cannot represent two grants of one spell at different ranks.
proficiency.whatIsMissing: The Spells page shows one Silence, castable once per day at 1st rank. The feat gives two castings a day — one at 1st rank and one at 2nd. The 2nd-rank casting (the one that actually matters, since 2nd-rank Silence is the useful version) never appears, and the per-day count is 1 instead of 2.
proficiency.suggestedField: Key the dedup at build.ts:2740 by spellId + effective cast rank (or merge same-spellId grants by summing usesPerDay and keeping every distinct rank), so InnateSpellGrant's existing `rank` field can carry two entries for one spell. Alternatively express it as a single grant with usesPerDay 2 plus a note, which loses the rank split but at least restores the second casting.

proficiency.quote: You gain the Sun's Fury focus spell. If you don't already have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point
proficiency.reason: The auditor's own reason documents the defect and then declines to file it — while filing the IDENTICAL defect as a MISS on crystal-ward-spells. I confirmed the field is not merely mis-ordered but structurally unreachable for this record's shape. build.ts:2512-2521 collects spellcastingGrants, and the ONLY consumer is the 'innate-casting' entry pushed at build.ts:2777-2789 — which sits inside `if (innate.length)` (build.ts:2741). suns-fury grants no innate spell (core.json feats.suns-fury has focusSpells:['suns-fury'] and no innateSpells), so on a character with no other innate grant the profile is applied to nothing at all. The focus entry that DOES exist is built at build.ts:1940-1962 with a hardcoded `proficiency:'trained'` and focusTradition/focusKey resolved only from grantOptions, focusCls.spellcasting, FOCUS_CASTING (build.ts:1265 — champion/monk/ranger only) or `focusCls.keyAbility[0]`; it never looks at spellcastingGrants. bright-lion-dedication is not in CASTER_ARCHETYPES either (grep: it appears only in featGrantsAuto.ts:59 and situationalBonuses.ts:110), so no divine/Cha caster entry exists to inherit from. Carrying an inert field is not the same as reaching the sheet, and the number that reaches the sheet is wrong, not absent.
proficiency.whatIsMissing: On any non-Charisma host the Sun's Fury spell attack roll and Focus DC use the wrong attribute and tradition — a fighter Bright Lion (classes.fighter.keyAbility[0]==='dex') gets a Dexterity-keyed, 'occult' Focus DC instead of the Charisma-keyed divine one the feat grants. Worse, on a host that DOES have unrelated innate spells (a seer elf, say) the divine/Cha profile is applied to the innate entry it has nothing to do with, and still not to the focus entry.
proficiency.suggestedField: Same fix as crystal-ward-spells: move the spellcastingGrants collection (build.ts:2512) above the focus-entry construction (build.ts:1940) and let a grant override focusTradition/focusKey/proficiency for the entry whose focus spells came from that feat (featFocusSpells already tracks provenance via focusSource). Filing crystal-ward-spells as a MISS and suns-fury as already-modelled hides half the fix.

proficiency.quote: As long as you have The Trader invested, you gain a +2 item bonus to Diplomacy checks made to Gather Information. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.
proficiency.reason: The passive bonus is registered: FEAT_SITUATIONAL 'the-trader' at situationalBonuses.ts:1507 ({skill:'diplomacy'}, when 'to Gather Information', '+2 item (+3 at 17th level)'), and core.json items.the-trader carries frequency {max:1, per:'day'} with counters [{id:'freq', per:'day', resetsOnRest:true}] for the activation. Residual, same class of limitation as the silvertongue mode: 'select two skills. Your proficiency rank with those two skills swaps for 1 hour' has no picker and moves no rank, because a mode modifier cannot target two player-chosen skills.

proficiency.quote: Choose an uncommon simple or martial weapon with a trait corresponding to an ancestry (such as dwarf, goblin, or orc) or that is common in another culture.
proficiency.reason: The `choice` field is present, but I grepped src/ for its flag and it is read NOWHERE: `grep -rn "unconventionalWeapon" src/` returns zero hits (the string exists only in public/core.json). So the pick is stored and displayed and nothing consumes it — which the record itself confesses via `choice.inert`: 'Recorded only: access and the treat-as-simple (or treat-as-martial) proficiency are not applied to your sheet.' That confession is the point: in the PROFICIENCY lane, the record's entire mechanical content is a proficiency treatment, and it does not reach the sheet. This is not the 'legacy pick, warn it grants nothing' case either — the effect IS expressible with primitives the engine already ships: proficiencies.weaponOverrides is written from weaponFamiliarity at build.ts:2455-2472, and build.ts:2465 already resolves a grant FROM THE PLAYER'S CHOICE VALUE (`g?.choiceGrants?.[fc.choice.value]?.weaponFamiliarity`, the Viking Shieldbearer case). The only new thing needed is reading the open choice's value as the weapon id instead of looking it up in a fixed map.
proficiency.whatIsMissing: A human fighter who takes Unconventional Weaponry for, say, an urumi still shows that weapon at its real category — no simple-weapon (or martial-weapon) treatment — so the Strike's attack modifier is computed from the wrong category rank, or the weapon is unusable at untrained. The number on the Strikes list does not move at all when the pick is made.
proficiency.suggestedField: src/rules/build.ts weaponFamiliarity block (2455-2472): after the existing choiceGrants lookup, handle an open weapon choice — for a feat registered with e.g. { weaponFamiliarityFromChoice: { flag: 'unconventionalWeapon', useCategoryRank: 'simple' } } set weaponOverrides[chosenWeaponId] = maxRank(existing, proficiencies.attacks.simple) (and .martial for the advanced-weapon branch). Then drop the `inert` string, since the pick would no longer be recorded-only. The same shape unlocks unconventional-expertise, which core.json shows carries no engine fields either.

proficiency.quote: You gain a +1 status bonus to your spell attack rolls against your hunted prey, and they take a –1 status penalty to their saving throws against divine spells you cast. You gain the Vindicator's Mark warden spell.
proficiency.reason: Four separate wirings. (1) core.json classFeatures.vindicator carries choice {flag:'tracklessTerrain', kind:'array', options:[natural, urban]} for the 5th-level Trackless Journey clause. (2) FEAT_SITUATIONAL 'vindicator' at situationalBonuses.ts:903 encodes the vindication-edge bonus including the Masterful Hunter upgrade ({kind:'spell', detail:'attack'}, '+1 status (+2 from 17th level with Masterful Hunter)'), and 'vindicator-dedication' at :383 covers the Religion social clause. (3) Vindicator's Mark IS granted: classes.ranger.subclass.options['vindicator'].focusSpells === ['vindicators-mark'], which build.ts:1900 folds into the focus repertoire and build.ts:1963 counts as a pool point. (4) The class-archetype layer adds the feature itself — feats.vindicator-dedication.classArchetype = {classId:'ranger', addFeatures:[{level:1, featureId:'vindicator'}], note:'…'}, applied at build.ts:2410-2426. The Religion-instead-of-Nature, favored-weapon and Deadly Simplicity substitutions ship as that classArchetype `note` (surfaced to the player as a note, not applied as numbers) — a deliberate, displayed limitation of the substitute lane.

defense.reason: It IS wired as a battle form: core.json `stances` bucket has an entry keyed `a-little-bird-told-me` with `form: true`, `senses: [low-light-vision, scent imprecise 30]`, `speeds: {fly: 25}`, and a note carrying the AC=20+level / weakness 5 physical / Acrobatics+Stealth +10 text. derive.ts:717-719 pushes the active stance's senses and speeds into the sheet. Calling it merely 'examined' understated it.
defense.quote: You become Tiny, gain the animal trait, and you can't make Strikes... Fly speed 25 feet. Weakness 5 to physical damage. Low-light vision and imprecise scent 30 feet.

defense.reason: Carries `counters` + `frequency` (confirmed on the core.json item record), which is the whole mechanical surface it needs: both activations are frequency-limited. The fascination lands on other creatures (target-side, Bomber's-Eye ruling) and 'Dive!' creates a Bathysphere vehicle, which the app already ships as a companion-type vehicle.
defense.quote: **Frequency** once per hour **Effect** All creatures within the bright light of the *submersible anglerfish lantern* must succeed at a save or be fascinated by the light for 1 round

defense.reason: Registered in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2015 with two targets — {kind:'ac'} and {kind:'save', detail:'all'} — condition 'against attacks and spells that deal fire damage', bonus '+1 circumstance'. The sheet stars AC and saves and lists the condition.
defense.quote: Wearing armor made from grisantian pelt also grants you a +1 circumstance bonus to your AC and saving throws against attacks and spells that deal fire damage.

defense.reason: Doubly wired: the item carries `uses`, AND core.json `modes` has `item-aurochs-jerky` (fromItemId aurochs-jerky, duration '1 hour') with modifier {target:'save', detail:'fortitude', type:'item', value:1}; its note documents the separate Aurochs' Endurance activation. It also appears in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts.
defense.quote: During this time, you gain a +1 item bonus to Fortitude saves.

defense.reason: The verdict is defended entirely by the `effectChoices` picker, and that picker is real — I dumped it: one menu id 'mutation' with 8 options (fly, amphibious, resist-acid/cold/electricity/fire/void/sonic) carrying genuine grants. But the feat's text has TWO independent effects, and the picker covers only the second one. The first sentence — "You gain low-light vision or darkvision, if one is appropriate for creatures with those traits" — is an unmodelled sense grant. grantsFeat.quote: When you use Kobold Breath, you can increase the damage dice to d8s and increase the area to 60 feet for a line breath weapon or 30 feet for a cone. If you do, you can't use Kobold Breath again for 1 hour.
grantsFeat.reason: The "entirely HP or damage" exemption was applied to the wrong surface. The owner's ruling governs STAT rows; the app has a dedicated registry for effects that change no stat but change an ACTION — src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2599 RECORD_MARKERS, whose own header says "Magic Hands makes Treat Wounds heal d10s instead of d8s… none of those has a stat row". Two of its six current entries are precisely this shape: "magic-hands" → {on:'action', id:'treat-wounds', value:'d10'} (a damage/healing DICE-SIZE change) and "black-powder-boost" → {on:'action', id:'leap', value:'+10 feet'} (a DISTANCE change). Dragon's Breath is both at once: dice to d8s and area to a 60-ft line / 30-ft cone. The lookup is reachable: src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:410 calls recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'action', actionId(a.name)) where actionId (MainTab.tsx:171) is just the SLUG OF THE ROW'S NAME, so a feat-derived action row works — Kobold Breath is a 2-action feat (core.json feats['kobold-breath'].actionCost {type:'actions',value:2}) and renders as the row "Kobold Breath" → slug 'kobold-breath'. It does not need to be in the actions collection. core.json feats['dragons-breath'] carries only {"edition":"legacy"}, and 'dragons-breath' appears nowhere in src/ (grepped RECORD_MARKERS, FEAT_SITUATIONAL, all featGrants*/featPickGrants/featFeatGrants, the modes bucket). The record is also live by default — edition 'legacy' is hidden only when the player turns on the remaster-only toggle (build.ts:1135-1152), and it is not edition 'superseded'.
grantsFeat.whatIsMissing: The Kobold Breath row on the sheet shows the unmodified breath with no indication the character can upgrade it, and there is no star back to Dragon's Breath — the same silence RECORD_MARKERS was built to remove for Magic Hands. Secondarily the 1-hour lockout is a trackable per-period limit the app can render as pips (1/hour) and does not.
grantsFeat.suggestedField: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts → RECORD_MARKERS['dragons-breath'] = [{ on: 'action', id: 'kobold-breath', value: 'd8s; 60-ft line / 30-ft cone', note: "You can increase Kobold Breath's damage dice to d8s and its area to a 60-foot line or 30-foot cone; if you do, you can't use Kobold Breath again for 1 hour." }]; optionally also core.json feats['dragons-breath'].limitedUses = {max:1, per:'hour'} — featUses.ts already supports per:'hour' (see effectiveUses / usesLabel) and core.json uses that cadence elsewhere (call-ursine-ally: limitedUses {max:1, per:'hour'}).

grantsFeat.quote: When you gain an ancestry feat, you can choose from dromaar and orc feats in addition to those from your ancestry.
grantsFeat.reason: The `senses` field covers only the low-light-vision clause (record is {ancestryId:null, versatile:true, senses:[low-light-vision]}). `versatile:true` is NOT feat access — grepping every use of `versatile` shows it only marks 'any ancestry may take this heritage' (homebrewSchemas.ts:298-305 round-trips it to the '__versatile__' ancestryId option). Feat eligibility is gated solely by featSlots.ts:56 on build.ancestryId, and featSlots.ts never mentions heritageId. core.json has 4 feats carrying the 'dromaar' trait (orc-sight, tusks-half-orc, overlooked-mastermind, monstrous-peacemaker), all category 'ancestry', and there is no 'dromaar' ancestry.
grantsFeat.suggestedField: src/rules/featSlots.ts eligibleFeatsForSlot (line 56) widened by a new Heritage.extraFeatTraits field in public/core.json — dromaar would carry ['dromaar','orc']
grantsFeat.whatIsMissing: A pick the builder never offers, and it is worse than the half-elf case: the heritage's OWN four feats are unreachable. A human or dwarf Dromaar can never select orc-sight or tusks-half-orc, because the ancestry picker only shows feats carrying their base ancestry trait. This applies to all 22 versatile heritages in core.json.

grantsFeat.quote: Your Point Out actions lose the auditory trait, and you don't need to be heard to convey the information to your allies. In addition, a creature you Point Out is off-guard to your allies until the start of your next turn.
grantsFeat.reason: "Removing a trait from an action changes no number" is true but not the test — RECORD_MARKERS exists for marks that carry only a note (RecordMarker.value is explicitly optional: "Omitted when there is no single value to show and the mark is only the note", situationalBonuses.ts:2585-2596). And this one is not invisible on the sheet: Point Out is a rendered action row with its traits printed — src/rules/actions.ts:44 { name: 'Point Out', mode: 'encounter', cost: A1, traits: ['auditory','manipulate','visual'] } — so today an investigator with this feat reads 'auditory' on their own Point Out row when the feat says it is gone (and that they no longer need to be heard, which matters while deafened, silenced, or in a silence effect). That is a wrong displayed value on the character's OWN sheet, not a number on a target and not an ally-side bonus. The marker is directly expressible and reachable: MainTab.tsx:410 keys the lookup on actionId(a.name) → 'point-out'. Confirmed absent: grep for 'empiricists-eye' and 'point-out' across src/ returns only actions.ts:44 and skillActions.ts:682 — no RECORD_MARKERS, FEAT_SITUATIONAL, or any other registry entry, and core.json feats['empiricists-eye'] carries only {"edition":"remaster-era"}. The off-guard-to-allies and Blind-Fight-for-allies clauses ARE correctly exempt (ruling F); the trait removal is a separate clause that lands on the character.
grantsFeat.whatIsMissing: A trait the sheet still shows and shouldn't. The Point Out row keeps 'auditory' and there is no mark linking it to the feat, so the one clause that changes the character's own action is invisible — the player has to remember the feat rewrote an action the sheet renders for them.
grantsFeat.suggestedField: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts → RECORD_MARKERS['empiricists-eye'] = [{ on: 'action', id: 'point-out', note: "Your Point Out loses the auditory trait and you don't need to be heard; the creature you Point Out is also off-guard to your allies until the start of your next turn." }]

grantsFeat.quote: **Tradition** primal (but see Fey Gift Spells below) **Traits** eidolon, fey … **Senses** low-light vision **Speed** 25 feet

grantsFeat.reason: Carries both halves. core.json feats['foxfire'] has choice = {flag:'damage', options:[electricity, fire, cold]} AND grantedStrikes = [{name:'Foxfire', die:'d4', damageType:'{item|flags…rulesSelections.damage}', traits:['unarmed','magical'], group:'sling', range:20}]. build.ts:1012 consumes it — `push(content.feats[f.featId]?.grantedStrikes, f.choice?.value)` — passing the choice value in precisely so the placeholder damage type resolves to the pick. grantsFeat.reason: Carries `effectChoices` in full: five entries (spell-1…spell-5), each an open spellFilter with traditions all four, the right rank bounds (minRank 1/maxRank 2 for the first three, rank 3 with minLevel 14, rank 4 with minLevel 20), and grantAs:'innate' with innate:{atWill:true, heightenHalfLevel:true} — which encodes the 'heightened to a rank equal to half your level' clause. Both the level-gating and the heightening are modelled, not just the pick.

grantsFeat.quote: You gain the Energized Spark feat for your choice of sonic or vitality.
grantsFeat.reason: core.json classFeatures['of-verse-unbroken'] carries only {otherTags:['exemplar-dominion-epithet'], critSpec:true} — no grantsFeats and no choice. build.ts:2205 already reads content.classFeatures[id]?.grantsFeats, and the target feat core.json feats['energized-spark'] exists (level 1, category class, with its own 12-option damage-type choice). Not present in featFeatGrants.ts, featGrants.ts, featGrantsAuto.ts, featGrantsLane.ts, featPickGrants.ts or situationalBonuses.ts (grepped for both ids).
grantsFeat.suggestedField: public/core.json classFeatures['of-verse-unbroken'].grantsFeats = ['energized-spark'], with the granted feat's choice narrowed to ['sonic','vitality']

grantsFeat.quote: You gain either the Combat Climber or Underwater Marauder skill feat, even if you do not meet its prerequisites. You have familiarity with the following weapons: Hatchet, Rapier, Scimitar, and Whip—for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these weapons as simple weapons.
grantsFeat.reason: One of three clauses is wired. core.json carries critSpec:true, critSpecLevel:5, critSpecWeapons:{bases:['hatchet','rapier','scimitar','whip']} — that covers the 5th-level critical-specialization sentence. But (a) the `choice` field only RECORDS combat-climber/underwater-marauder; nothing turns the recorded value into a granted feat (FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS is unconditional-only per its header, and there is no FEAT_GRANTS['pirate-combat-training'].choiceGrants — the id appears nowhere in featGrants.ts/featGrantsAuto.ts/featGrantsLane.ts/featFeatGrants.ts/featPickGrants.ts), and (b) no weaponFamiliarity entry exists for the four named weapons.
grantsFeat.suggestedField: src/rules/featGrants.ts → FEAT_GRANTS['pirate-combat-training'] with weaponFamiliarity:{weapons:['hatchet','rapier','scimitar','whip'], rank:'trained'}, and a feat lane on choiceGrants (or a FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS variant keyed by choice value) for the Combat Climber / Underwater Marauder branch

(1) A character with only simple-weapon training who takes this feat is owed trained proficiency with a rapier or scimitar; deriveStrike still reads their untrained martial rank, so the attack bonus is short by the full proficiency step. (2) The chosen skill feat is recorded in the dropdown but never granted, so it is absent from Feats & Features and Combat Climber's climb effects never apply.

grantsFeat.quote: You gain a skill feat and the rogue's Surprise Attack class feature. You become trained in light armor. In addition, you become trained in Stealth or Thievery plus one skill of your choice … You become trained in rogue class DC.
grantsFeat.reason: Fully wired across a registry and two record fields. src/rules/featGrants.ts:198 HAND_AUTHORED_GRANTS['rogue-dedication'] = { armor:{light:'trained'}, skillChoices:[{options:['stealth','thievery'],rank:'trained'},{options:'any',rank:'trained'}], bonusSkillFeat:true } — bonusSkillFeat is documented (featGrants.ts:121-126) as injecting an extra skill-feat slot for exactly this sentence. core.json adds choice (stealth/thievery) and classDcGrant:{classId:'rogue'}, consumed at build.ts:2493. Surprise Attack itself needs nothing — it makes the TARGET off-guard on the first round, which the owner ruled the player tells the GM.

grantsFeat.quote: You gain the Shall not Falter, Shall not Rout focus spell. If you don't already have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point … Your knight reclaimant focus spells are divine spells; when you gain this feat, you become trained in divine spell attacks and spell DCs and your spellcasting ability is Charisma.
grantsFeat.reason: Carries both engine fields the text needs: focusSpells:['shall-not-falter-shall-not-rout'] (which also carries its own Focus Point, per the Feat.focusSpells contract) and spellcastingGrant:{tradition:'divine', keyAbility:'cha', proficiency:'trained'} — matching the divine/Charisma/trained sentence exactly.

grantsFeat.quote: The animal companion you gain from the Animal Trainer Dedication feat gains one specialization of your choice. Increase its proficiency rank in Performance to legendary instead of one of the specialization's skill increases.
grantsFeat.reason: Registered in a registry: src/rules/companionGrants.ts:172 — 'specialized-companion-animal-trainer': {"kinds":["animal"],"maturityFloor":"specialized","note":"Animal Trainer companion: gains one specialization of your choice, and its Performance proficiency is legendary in place of one of the specialization's skill increases."}. maturityFloor:'specialized' raises the companion's maturity so the specialization picker opens; the Performance swap is carried as the note.

grantsFeat.quote: At 3rd level, 7th level, and 15th level, you gain an additional skill increase you can apply only to Acrobatics or the skill from your swashbuckler's style.
grantsFeat.reason: The skill-FEAT half of the feature is baked in — core.json classes['swashbuckler'].featProgression.skill = [2,3,4,6,7,8,10,12,14,15,16,18,20], i.e. the standard even levels PLUS 3, 7 and 15, which are precisely this feature's three bonus feats. The skill-INCREASE half is not: classes['swashbuckler'].skillIncreaseLevels = [3,5,7,9,11,13,15,17,19] — the plain 9-entry default (identical to seed.ts:111), with no duplicate entries for 3/7/15. And a duplicate could not work anyway: build.ts:1355-1363 iterates levels and reads `build.skillIncreases[lvl]`, one increase per LEVEL, so a second increase at level 3 has nowhere to be stored. core.json classFeatures['stylish-tricks'] itself is empty ({}).
grantsFeat.suggestedField: a bonus-increase lane the level-keyed store can express — e.g. Class.extraSkillIncreaseLevels plus a second key in BuildState.skillIncreases (build.ts:1355) — or classFeatures['stylish-tricks'].grants carrying the three increases
grantsFeat.whatIsMissing: Three numbers that never move. A 15th-level swashbuckler is owed 3 skill increases beyond the standard progression (restricted to Acrobatics or their style skill) and receives 0, so up to three skills sit a full proficiency rank low for the whole build. The restriction on both the extra increases and the extra skill feats is also unenforced.

grantsFeat.quote: You gain a skill feat: Charming Liar if you chose Deception or Hobnobber if you chose Diplomacy.
grantsFeat.reason: The `choice` in engineFieldsPresent is NOT this clause — I dumped the record from public/core.json and choice = {flag:'gebCityLore', prompt:'Geb city Lore', options:[Graydirge/Mechitar/Yled Lore]}, which serves the separate Lore sentence. The record has no grantedFeatId and no grantedFeatByChoice, and types.ts:601 documents grantedFeatByChoice as the field for exactly this shape ('The feat depends on which trainedSkillChoice you took'). backgroundGrantedFeats() (build.ts:342) therefore returns nothing here. Charming Liar and Hobnobber appear only as inert descRefs.

The background grants a skill feat keyed to the skill you picked; the app applies the skill training and the Lore, then drops the feat — so Charming Liar/Hobnobber never appear in Feats & Features, and Charming Liar's own situational Deception effect never registers.

spellGrant.quote: You gain a single 10th-rank spell slot and can prepare a spell in that slot using animist spellcasting.
spellGrant.reason: Record carries no mechanical field (verified in public/core.json: only description/source/prereqs). The animist's slot table src/rules/spellcasting.ts animistPreparedSlots() loops `for (let r = 1; r <= 9; r++)` and never emits rank 10, and unlike fullCasterSlots() it has no `if (level >= 19) slots[10] = 1` line. The existing SpellSlotBonus type (types.ts:357) only supports perRank/exceptHighest, so even a naive backfill cannot express 'one slot at rank 10'.
spellGrant.suggestedField: spellSlotBonus on the feat (extended with a rank-specific form), or gate a `slots[10] = 1` in animistPreparedSlots on the feat being taken
spellGrant.whatIsMissing: A 20th-level animist who takes this feat gets no 10th-rank slot row on the Spells page — the number of slots does not move at all.

spellGrant.quote: Choose a deity. You are bound by your deity's anathema and gain the champion's aura and sanctification as described in the champion class. Choose a cause as you would if you were a champion… You become trained in Religion and your deity's associated skill… You become trained in champion class DC.

spellGrant.suggestedField: classDcGrant: {classId:'champion'} on the feat; an effectChoices/choice for the cause; extend buildNeedsDeity to archetype dedications so the deity's associated skill is trained
spellGrant.whatIsMissing: Two picks the builder never offers (deity, cause) and two numbers that never move: champion class DC stays untrained, and the deity's associated skill is never trained.

spellGrant.quote: When you first gain a ki spell, decide whether your ki spells are divine spells or occult spells.
spellGrant.reason: The record is DEAD DATA — nothing you put on it is ever read. `classFeatures/ki-spells` is referenced by no class: `core.json classes.monk.features` has 18 entries (mystic-strikes, flurry-of-blows, powerful-fist, monk-expertise, graceful-legend, …) and none is `ki-spells`; `JSON.stringify(c.classes).includes('ki-spells')` is false; the only reference anywhere in `src/` or `core.json` is the record itself (featFeatGrants.ts:153/225 grant `qi-spells`, the FEAT, not this feature). So no character ever owns it and an `effectChoices` added here would be inert. Everything else in it is also delivered elsewhere for a monk who does have qi spells (FOCUS_CASTING monk = occult/Wis at build.ts:1267, spell attack/DC advancement via monk-expertise/graceful-legend, focus pool via each focusSpells grant). And the divine-or-occult sentence is LEGACY CRB text the Remaster dropped: the replacement is `feats/qi-spells` (Player Core 2, edition 'remaster'), whose printed text is only "You gain Inner Upheaval, Qi Rush, or another 1st-rank monk qi spell" — no tradition choice — and the remaster qi spells themselves carry `traditions: []`. Separately (not this record, and not this lane): the live gap is that `feats/qi-spells` / `advanced-qi-spells` / `master-qi-spells` / `grandmaster-qi-spells` carry NO focusSpells / effectChoices, so the "choose a monk qi spell" pick is never offered and a monk who takes Qi Spells gets no focus spell and no pool — that is where work should go, and it is a choice-lane miss, not a tradition one.

spellGrant.quote: While the relic's fervor gift lasts, you have access to the spell provided by the emotional state, which you can cast using your own spell slots.
spellGrant.reason: Record carries no field (verified: keys are id/name/traits/rarity/source/description/level/bulk/itemType/edition only). Relic gifts ARE modelled by id where they carry numbers — FEAT_SITUATIONAL has heavens-grace, fiendish-bargain, jet-propulsion, work-harden, wind-barrier at situationalBonuses.ts:1930-2011 — this one is absent. The emotional-state→spell table is not in the data, which is exactly the shape the project already handles with `dataWarning`: cathartic-focus-spell carries 'grants the focus spell listed under your catharsis emotion — the Cathartic Mage emotion entries … missing'. Only 5 records in core.json use dataWarning and this is not one of them.
spellGrant.suggestedField: dataWarning at minimum; properly, effectChoices (one option per emotional fervor) granting heldSpells

The registry has the exact vocabulary for it: SituationalTarget.kind includes 'strikeDamage' and 'spellDamage' (situationalBonuses.ts:24-36), added precisely because damage bonuses "had nowhere to be stored", and entries like kortos-diamond (:2225) already store "+2d8 damage". feats['ignite-the-sun'] carries no engine field and appears in no registry.

resource.quote: Your familiar gains the Patron's Presence activity.
resource.reason: The load-bearing half of the reason is factually false. The audit wrote "its limiter is 'Frequency once per hour', not a per-day pool, so `uses`/`counters` have nothing to hold" — but `limitedUses` is per-period, not per-day: core.json carries limitedUses on 452 feats, of which 127 are `per:'hour'` (sacred-defense, verdant-presence, feed-on-pain, spore-cloud, nanite-surge, critter-shape…), and featUses.ts treats 'hour' as SUB_DAILY so it refills on the encounter reset (featUses.ts:107). The "it's the FAMILIAR's ability, not yours" objection also fails on precedent: 5 feats already carry limitedUses for an ability that belongs to the familiar/companion (siphon-power, caterwaul, fulu-familiar, guarded-domain, adventurous-outfitter). feats['patrons-presence'] carries no field, appears in no registry, and the granted actions['patrons-presence'] carries no uses either (0 records in the actions bucket carry `uses`/`frequency`), so the once-per-hour pool exists nowhere on the sheet. The target-side stupefied is correctly exempt — the POOL is not.
resource.whatIsMissing: No use pips for the aura: the once-per-hour limit on Patron's Presence is text the player has to remember, while 127 other per-hour feats draw a spendable battery chip in the Feats tab.
resource.suggestedField: feats['patrons-presence'].limitedUses = { max: 1, per: 'hour' } (renders via featUse() at src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:295)

resource.quote: It gains the Primal Howl advanced maneuver, in addition to any advanced maneuvers it already knows.
resource.reason: Same false premise: "limited to 'once per hour' (no per-day pool)". actions['primal-howl'].description opens with "**Frequency** once per hour", and 127 feats already store exactly that as limitedUses{per:'hour'}. The companion-owns-it objection is answered by caterwaul / fulu-familiar / guarded-domain, which carry limitedUses for a familiar-or-companion ability. feats['primal-howl'] carries no engine field and is in no registry; the actions record carries no uses field either. The audit's own escape hatch — "the effect is entirely damage/condition on others" — covers the howl's damage and Frightened, but not the resource that limits how often it can be used.

companion.quote: Once placed, an oculus grants you constant Darkvision. ... If you already know the planar binding ritual, you gain a +3 item bonus on the primary check when casting planar binding.
companion.reason: I confirmed two of their three claims and disproved the third. Claim 1 verified on both surfaces: scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:4064-4075 is real, and the built public/core.json record carries passiveEffects.senses plus a top-level senses entry; I additionally checked the gate they did not, src/rules/derive.ts:708-715, which admits item passives when inv.worn || inv.invested || inv.equipped, and usage is 'held-in-one-hand', so the darkvision genuinely reaches the sheet. Claim 2 verified verbatim at src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:1195. Claim 3 is false: they wrote that 'the three-per-day, once-per-week and once-per-year pools are tracked', but only two counters exist. That false statement is load-bearing for their verdict — it is the sentence that lets a modellable, engine-expressible use pool pass as already handled and never get fixed. Their companion-lane reasoning is correct and I do not fault it: the 3-action see-through-your-companion's-eyes activation REQUIRES a familiar rather than granting one, and is an action taken at the table with no lasting sheet number, so the companion lane itself needs nothing. The overturn is narrow and not about the companion aspect: the record is one of the better-wired items in the file, but it is not complete, so 'already-modelled' is the wrong verdict. Note the missing pool is not excused by the target-side rule — the mass Suggestion's EFFECT is entirely on the targets and rightly needs nothing, but its once-per-year use limit is a number on the owner's own sheet, and this very item already tracks its other two limits there.
companion.whatIsMissing: (a) The once-per-year activation has NO use pool. public/core.json items['oculus-of-abaddon'].counters holds exactly two entries — freq (max 3, per day, resetsOnRest true) and freq2 (max 1, per week, resetsOnRest false) — while the text states three separate Frequency lines: 'three times per day' (Scrying), 'once per week' (Binding Circle) and 'once per year' (the 1-mile Suggestion). A third counter {id:'freq3', label:'per year', max:1, per:'year', resetsOnRest:false} is needed. It requires no engine change: ItemCounter.per is an unconstrained `per?: string` (src/rules/types.ts:1044) and resetsOnRest is author-set per counter, exactly as freq2 already proves for the per-week pool. Nothing else covers it — because `counters` is present, counterDefs in src/rules/itemUses.ts:25-31 never falls through to the `frequency` fallback. (b) Secondary, same record: heldSpells is {2:['darkvision'], 4:['suggestion'], 6:['scrying','binding-circle']}. build.ts:2666-2676 reads those keys as cast-at ranks and builds a real item spellcasting entry from them, so two defects surface on the Spells page — 'darkvision' is listed as a castable rank-2 spell although the item grants Darkvision only as a CONSTANT sense (already correctly held in passiveEffects.senses), i.e. a castable ability the item does not have; and scrying/binding-circle sit at rank 6, their base ranks, while the text heightens both to 7th, so the item's spells are cast one rank low.
